title: Touring with Cavallo, reading problems and back to the Salt City Six
summary: Weeklong lounge engagements, 75 dollars a week, difficulty reading jazz, then a return to the Salt City Six before 1965.

bands.name: Jimmy Cavallo and the House Rockers

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: What did being “on the road” constitute? Like one nighters in dance clubs?

No, well like depending on which band I was with — I went on the road with Jimmy Cavallo and we were playing weeklong engagements. We were like a week at the Thunderbird Lounge and wherever, New Bedford, Massachusetts, the Piccadilly Lounge. I remember they used to have a tank of piranha that was the high point of the evening, because we’d play on top of the bar and the bartender would feed the piranha something. I don’t know what he was feeding them, goldfish I guess. And that was fun. But that was a club that was booking with Sonny Stitt one week and then Jimmy Cavallo, like we’re there, and this and that. And then we’d do Lancaster, we’d do Hazelton, Thunderbird Lounge, I can’t remember the name of all the places. But the bread was so light, you know it was just no bread at all. I made $75 a week, but I mean still it was better than — I was getting my experience anyway. But I wasn’t getting any reading experience you see. And even though I had played tympani and played Grade 6 drum solos, things like that during high school, I mean I went to all-state you know down at the Concord Hotel and all this and that. But that kind of reading was different than reading jazz music. Because when you read an eighth note [scats] but if you read an eighth note in jazz it’s like [scats],

you know, like you’re hearing the syncopation. I see an eighth note and it’s like baDA, not bada. You know, so that kind of thing. So I wasn’t really locked into that. Now I quit Jimmy Cavallo’s band and went back with the Salt City Six for a couple of years I guess. And we were traveling doing Florida, and I don’t remember the places, whatever they were. And those were nice jobs. But in 1965 Vietnam was heating up.
